extracted.intended_audience: Users and programmers of the MetaPost language (people writing or running MetaPost programs; TeX/graphics users)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference/specification for writing, running, and porting MetaPost programs: command-line usage, language grammar (BNF), operators/commands, macros, and compatibility notes with METAFONT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command-line syntax for mpost
rubrics_metrics.description: The MetaPost executable is invoked as: mpost [⟨switches⟩] [&⟨preloadfile⟩] [⟨infile⟩] [⟨commands⟩]. Any parameter is optional; with no arguments MetaPost enters interactive mode (prompt '**').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All text after ⟨infile⟩ is interpreted as MetaPost code and processed after the file is read. If neither ⟨infile⟩ nor ⟨commands⟩ contain an end statement, MetaPost enters interactive mode after processing input. Example: 'mpost -tex=latex fig' compiles fig.mp using LaTeX for btex/etex labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input file resolution rules (⟨infile⟩)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ⟨infile⟩ doesn't end with .mp, MetaPost first looks for ⟨infile⟩.mp; only if that doesn't exist does it look for ⟨infile⟩ literally. If ⟨infile⟩ ends with .mp, it is used as given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If both 'fig' and 'fig.mp' exist and you call 'mpost fig', 'fig.mp' is processed. To process the file literally named 'fig' in that case, invoke 'mpost fig.' (trailing dot). If no input file is found, MetaPost prints an error and interactively asks for a new name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preload file behavior (&⟨preloadfile⟩ and -ini)
rubrics_metrics.description: The code in &⟨preloadfile⟩ (and files it inputs) is executed before other processing; it should end with end or dump. By default MetaPost loads mpost.mp (or the executable's actual name) unless &⟨preloadfile⟩ or -mem is specified. Use -ini to suppress default preload behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use &mfplain to load mfplain macros before processing (example usage given). A preload file may initialize macros, variables, or formats required by the input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning and processing of ⟨commands⟩ on command-line
rubrics_metrics.description: All text on the command-line after ⟨infile⟩ is interpreted as MetaPost code and processed after ⟨infile⟩ is read. If ⟨infile⟩ already contains an end statement, ⟨commands⟩ are effectively ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no end statement appears either in file or commands, MetaPost enters interactive mode after processing all input.

rubrics_metrics.name: mpost switches and their semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: mpost supports many switches (either single- or double-dash). Notable switches and their behavior are documented: -debug, -dvitomp, -file-line-error, -halt-on-error, -help, -ini, -interaction=⟨string⟩, -jobname=⟨jobname⟩, -kpathsea-debug=⟨number⟩, -mem=⟨string⟩, -no-file-line-error, -no-kpathsea, -numbersystem=⟨string⟩, -progname=⟨string⟩, -recorder, -s ⟨key⟩=⟨value⟩, -tex=⟨texprogram⟩, -troff/-T, -version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and effects: -halt-on-error immediately exits on first error; -s can set internal variables before reading the input (e.g., -s 'outputformat="svg"' -s prologues=3); -tex=latex loads the tex program to typeset btex/etex labels. Some switches are silently ignored in mplib-based MetaPost (e.g., -8bit, -parse-first-line) and others are ignored but trigger warnings (e.g., -no-parse-first-line, -output-directory).

rubrics_metrics.name: dvitomp usage and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: dvitomp is a utility to convert DVI files into low-level MetaPost code with syntax: dvitomp [⟨switches⟩] ⟨infile⟩ [⟨outfile⟩]. If infile name doesn't end with .dvi, the extension is appended; dvitomp never opens files not ending with .dvi. If ⟨outfile⟩ omitted, it is ⟨infile⟩ with .dvi replaced by .mpx.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: dvitomp supports -help, -kpathsea-debug, -progname, -version. Since MetaPost v1.100, label conversion is handled internally by mpost and mpware tools are obsolete; dvitomp may be a wrapper calling 'mpost -dvitomp ⟨infile⟩ ⟨outfile⟩'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar / syntax for expressions (BNF)
rubrics_metrics.description: The language grammar is formally specified in BNF: productions for ⟨atom⟩, ⟨primary⟩, ⟨secondary⟩, ⟨tertiary⟩, ⟨subexpression⟩, ⟨expression⟩, ⟨path knot⟩, ⟨path join⟩, ⟨direction specifier⟩, ⟨basic path join⟩, etc., define valid expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grammar includes numeric/pair/path/picture/string/transform types, nullary/unary/binary operators, pseudo functions, and transformer suffixes (rotated, scaled, shifted, slanted, transformed, xscaled, yscaled, zscaled, reflectedabout, rotatedaround). The formal productions define operator precedence and allowed constructs (e.g., primary allows tuple forms like (num,num) and of-operator constructs). See Figures 57–60 for full productions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator classification and typing (nullary, unary, binops, of-operators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators are categorized: nullary ops (e.g., false, true, normaldeviate), unary ops (type, abs, angle, arclength, etc.), primary/secondary/tertiary binary operators (e.g., *, /, +, -, or, and, intersectionpoint, intersectiontimes), and 'of' operators (arctime, direction, glyph, penoffset, point, subpath, substring, ...). Each operator has specified argument and result types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the operators table for exact argument/result types and explanation. Example semantics: arctime/direction/directiontime/directionpoint relate to path timing/direction; dotprod is vector dot product; mexp and mlog represent scaled exp/ln functions; uniformdeviate/random functions documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commands and their semantics (drawing, file, tracing, color, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands are listed (addto, clip, closefrom, cutdraw, dashed, draw, drawarrow, drawdblarrow, errhelp, errmessage, filenametemplate, fill, filldraw, fontmapfile, interim, let, loggingall, message, newinternal, pickup, save, setbounds, shipout, show, special, tracingall, tracingnone, undraw, unfill, unfilldraw, withcmykcolor, withcolor, withgreyscale, withoutcolor, withpen, withpostscript, withprescript, withrgbcolor, write to). Each has a documented effect (drawing, file output, tracing, color application, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: draw draws a line or picture; fill fills inside a cyclic path; clip applies a clipping path; shipout outputs a figure; errmessage/errhelp declare runtime help messages. filenametemplate is deprecated in favor of outputtemplate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function-like macros and pseudo procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost provides function-like macros (incr, decr, dashpattern, buildcycle, thelabel..., image, etc.) and pseudo procedures (drawoptions, label variants, dotlabel variants, labels/dotlabels). Their argument types and results are specified (e.g., incr/decr operate on numeric variables and return numeric).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table lists each macro name, argument types, and result type. Use these macros for common patterns: dashpattern builds dashed-line patterns, buildcycle builds a cyclic path from path expressions, thelabel returns a picture for labeling, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program structure and statement syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: A MetaPost program is ⟨statement list⟩ end. Statements include equations, assignments, declarations, macro definitions, compounds (begingroup/endgroup, beginfig/endfig), pseudo procedures, and commands. Equations are of form ⟨expression⟩ = ⟨right-hand side⟩; assignments use :=.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Macro definitions use 'def' or 'vardef' headings and end with enddef. Declarations specify types and lists of variables. Compound statements create local scopes. The BNF defines how to construct well-formed programs (Figure 61).

rubrics_metrics.name: Control structures: conditionals and loops
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditionals use 'if ⟨boolean expression⟩: ⟨balanced tokens⟩ ⟨alternatives⟩ fi' with optional else/elseif. Loops include 'for' forms (for var = progression, for var = for_list, for var within picture_expression, forsuffixes ...) and 'forever'. Progressions support upto/downto/step ... until forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: for-list and suffix-list syntaxes are defined; balanced tokens must appear in conditionals. See Figure 64 for full productions and examples of 'for' progression syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command syntax details and drawing options
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed syntactic forms for commands are provided: clip ⟨picture variable⟩ to ⟨path expression⟩, interim ⟨internal var⟩ := ⟨rhs⟩, let ⟨symbolic token⟩ = ⟨symbolic token⟩, pickup ⟨expression⟩, randomseed assignment, save list, setbounds ⟨picture var⟩ to ⟨path⟩, shipout ⟨picture expr⟩, write ⟨string expr⟩ to ⟨string expr⟩, addto variants, drawing commands with option lists (withcolor, withrgbcolor, withcmykcolor, withgreyscale, withoutcolor, withprescript, withpostscript, withpen, dashed...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawing commands include draw ⟨picture expr⟩ ⟨option list⟩ and fill-type commands (fill, draw, filldraw, unfill, undraw, unfilldraw, drawarrow, drawdblarrow, cutdraw). Option lists are sequences of drawing options; addto provides ways to append to picture variables (also, contour, doublepath).

rubrics_metrics.name: MetaPost versus METAFONT compatibility and mfplain package
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences and compatibility notes: many METAFONT font-making primitives exist but are not defined in Plain MetaPost; a macro package mfplain exists to provide macros to process Computer Modern fonts. Some METAFONT primitives and internal variables are meaningless in MetaPost (display-related primitives, pixels_per_inch), and some primitives have different meanings (special behaves differently).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To use mfplain, preload it via '&mfplain' on the command line. The manual lists primitives present in MetaPost but not METAFONT and vice versa, plus macros defined only in mfplain. filenametemplate is deprecated in favor of outputtemplate — compatibility code examples are provided to support versions before/after 1.200.

rubrics_metrics.name: File-name template / outputtemplate behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost historically had filenametemplate primitive for output file naming; since version 1.200 outputtemplate (an internal string variable) supersedes it and supports %{...} escapes for internal variables. filenametemplate is deprecated but still supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
For portability across MetaPost versions 1.000–1.200, conditionally use filenametemplate vs outputtemplate based on mpversion; example conditional provided:
if scantokens(mpversion) < 1.200: filenametemplate "%j-%c.mps"; else: outputtemplate := "%j-%c.mps"; fi
